name: Jawbreaker
label: Tupelo
lede: Three Santa Monica kids who swore off major labels signed to DGC for a reported $1 million, then played to fans who sat down on the floor. Twenty-one years after the split, a festival put them back on a stage.

eras.title: Rise, then Jawbreaker
eras.text: Two Santa Monica friends land at NYU, answer a bassist's flyer and spend two years as Rise with the wrong singers. By 1989 they have a new name, a new frontman and a first show in Los Angeles.

years.h: Two Santa Monica friends reach NYU and answer a bassist's flyer
years.p: [[Chris Bauermeister|c6957066-0708-4f3b-9d43-5ce97c7ba645]] posted the flyer. He, [[Blake Schwarzenbach|c7d68007-b688-426f-a496-08467a0a6f44]] and [[Adam Pfahler|27a4001b-d621-40a6-aab8-6dd181b016ac]] rehearse at Giant Studios on Sixth Avenue as a band called Rise.
years.xp: Rise went through several singers. Then Schwarzenbach wrote and sang "Shield Your Eyes" for a demo. Jon Liu, one of the earlier vocalists, later said that was the song where everything worked.

years.h: Rise move to Los Angeles with Jon Liu on vocals
years.p: The move west comes in fall 1987. Liu keeps the mic until Schwarzenbach takes it over.

years.h: Rise becomes Jawbreaker, and Schwarzenbach takes over the singing
years.p: The name changes sometime in 1988 or 1989. The vocal job stays with him for good.

years.h: Jawbreaker plays its first show, at Club 88 in Los Angeles
years.p: March 16, 1989, under the new name.

eras.title: A broken-up tour, a move to the Mission, a voice going
eras.text: Two days in Venice for a debut, a van summer that ends in a breakup announcement, then San Francisco and a record made while Schwarzenbach's throat was failing.

years.h: Unfun gets two days in a Venice, California studio
years.p: Recorded in January 1990 and out in May on Shredder Records (SH-07). It is the debut album.
years.xp: Pfahler reissued a remastered Unfun on his own Blackball Records on March 30, 2010.

years.h: The "Fuck 90" tour ends with the band saying it's over
years.p: On the road with Econochrist, Bauermeister stops speaking to the other two when they reach Canada. By the last date, Jawbreaker says it is done.
years.xp:
Schwarzenbach later broke the tour down by the numbers: about six great shows and maybe 25 forgettable ones, in the kind of metal club you find in Florida.

He and Bauermeister went back to NYU. Pfahler regretted the split, and the three eventually made up in New York.

years.h: They move to the Mission, across the hall from Lance Hahn
years.p: Pfahler and Schwarzenbach share an apartment opposite Bauermeister and [[J Church|bad96c62-50f8-4159-b155-3ffb63c698f8]]'s Lance Hahn. [[Econochrist|bcaa3d82-4ac7-4977-a202-af30cc22c12a]] and [[Samiam|787aa69f-f419-4e24-8c13-33511a20428d]] adopt the newcomers.

years.h: Schwarzenbach records "Kiss the Bottle" ahead of throat surgery
years.p: It goes on the 17 Reasons Mission compilation, and his voice shows it. The song sketches the drinkers outside a Mission liquor store.
years.xp: Andy Greenwald, in Nothing Feels Good, calls it one of the band's best-loved songs, a working-class anthem with a steady heart. Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta has named it a favorite.

years.h: Billy Anderson engineers Bivouac, and the band stretches out
years.p: Released in December on Tupelo and Communion (TUP 38). Pfahler says the band was trying to prove something.

years.h: His voice goes in Europe, and Ireland means surgery
years.p: The throat trouble starts as Bivouac comes out. The surgery in Ireland stops the tour for a week.
years.xp: Schwarzenbach has described every day of that tour as dread: standing up there to see what would happen.

eras.title: Chicago, a cat and a label scouting from the Nirvana tour
eras.text: Tupelo gets two records. Steve Albini gets a credit that goes to his cat. Six Nirvana dates make the majors pay attention.

years.cap: Jawbreaker at Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, Aug. 7, 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: Jawbreaker (band) · mxdwn: Steve Albini Admits Confusing Jawbreaker with Jawbox in Teaser for Upcoming Documentary
years.h: Steve Albini records them in Chicago, and the credit goes to his cat
years.p: Most of 24 Hour Revenge Therapy is cut in May 1993, officially credited to Fluss, his cat. Billy Anderson adds three more tracks in San Francisco in August.
years.xp: Albini turns up in the teaser for the Jawbreaker documentary Don't Break Down, where he admits he used to confuse Jawbreaker with Jawbox.

years.cap: Adam Pfahler at Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, Aug. 7, 1993
years.h: Six dates opening for Nirvana on the In Utero tour
years.p: Thousands see them, and the rumor starts: a label has noticed. Someone does, and they get snapped up.
years.xp: Pfahler says people really came down on the band for touring with Nirvana. The prediction turned out right.

years.h: Tupelo releases 24 Hour Revenge Therapy on February 15
years.p: Catalog numbers TUP 49 and COMM 49. Andy Greenwald calls it arguably the band's best, Replacements-style regret played at Gilman Street speed.

years.cap: Jawbreaker at Jabberjaw, Los Angeles, Jan. 15, 1994
years.h: Ben Weasel said he'd eat his hat. Then Jawbreaker signed with DGC
years.p: Warner, Capitol and DGC all take meetings. The deal is said to be worth $1 million and turns on A&R man Mark Kates, who met them on the Nirvana tour and kept in touch.
years.xp: Ben Weasel of Screeching Weasel had promised to eat his hat if Jawbreaker ever signed to a major. He ran a photo of himself doing it in Maximumrocknroll.

eras.title: The major-label year
eras.text: They had sworn off the majors and then signed with one. Crowds sat down at their own shows, and about ten months after Dear You the band was finished.

years.h: Rob Cavallo gets six weeks of 12-hour days from Schwarzenbach
years.p: Fresh off [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]]'s Dookie, Cavallo has Bauermeister and Pfahler finished in three days at Fantasy Studios.
years.xp: Cavallo said Schwarzenbach really wanted to be heard, and decided to sing differently. Cavallo thought the songs could use some precision.

q: Pretty chilling. Like a muted acknowledgment.
years.src: Uproxx: Jawbreaker's Blake Schwarzenbach On 'Dear You' And Touring · Wikipedia: Dear You
years.h: Dear You comes out on DGC, and fans hear a voice sanded down
years.p: Schwarzenbach, on how the label received the record. DGC 24831, produced by Cavallo.
years.xp:
The clear vocals and glossy guitars split the fans who had trusted Schwarzenbach with their private lives. He told Uproxx the record felt more or less like silence for the next month.

DGC's feedback, he said, came from a world where selling 50,000 copies meant nobody would say anything to you.

years.h: MTV airs the "Fireman" video eight times
years.p: [[Green Day|084308bd-1654-436f-ba03-df6697104e19]] director Mark Kohr shoots three men in a tiny room at the Fox Oakland. Kates blames the band's lack of visual appeal.

years.h: Anti-Jawbreaker flyers follow the "Monsters of Jaw" tour with Jawbox
years.p: Activist Brian Zero hands them out, and some crowds sit down or turn their backs on the Dear You songs.
years.xp: Kates recalled the Roxy headline show: kids on the floor, backs to the stage during the new songs. Samiam's Sergie Loobkoff called a Warfield show in San Francisco a turning point. It was like no one cared.

years.h: Bauermeister and Schwarzenbach fight on a street in Salem, Oregon
years.p: By spring 1996 the two travel in separate vans. In Salem it turns physical and spills onto the street.
years.xp: Bauermeister remembered shouting at Schwarzenbach that he was a stupid son of a bitch who thinks it is all about him.

years.cap: Blake, Chris and Adam, c. 1996, in what is called the last photo of the band
years.h: Jawbreaker call it quits on the Fourth of July
years.p: About ten months after Dear You, the band ends after a run of unhappy dates.

eras.title: Brooklyn, a video store and a ten-year license
eras.text: Schwarzenbach heads to Brooklyn and Jets to Brazil, Pfahler opens a video store and a label, and Dear You comes back into print.

years.cap: Blake Schwarzenbach with Jets to Brazil
years.h: Schwarzenbach lands in Brooklyn with Jets to Brazil
years.p: [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]] mixes Britpop and piano ballads. Critics still fixated on his Jawbreaker past are "unspeakably scathing."

years.h: Pfahler opens Lost Weekend Video and starts Blackball Records
years.p: He stays in the Mission and plays in J Church with Lance Hahn from 1998 to 2002. Bauermeister goes back to his toy store job.
years.xp: Pfahler runs the Jawbreaker catalog through Blackball.

years.h: Live 4/30/96 puts the last tour on record
years.p: Recorded April 30, 1996 and released by Pfahler on Blackball as BB-002.

years.h: Pfahler pays $10,000 to get Dear You back in print
years.p: He licenses the album from Universal for ten years and Blackball issues it as a double LP with bonus tracks, including "Shirt." Copies had been selling for double the retail price.

years.h: Three men, one San Francisco studio, no cameras
years.p: The Don't Break Down filmmakers get all three together for the first time in 11 years. They play "Bivouac," "Condition Oakland" and "Parabola," and the audio is taken off the board.
years.xp: The band chose not to film it, out of respect for the sanctity of the moment and fear that they would suck, according to the account of the session.

eras.title: Blake said it would never happen
eras.text: For years he said he couldn't sing those songs. Then came a festival slot, a documentary and three nights at Brooklyn Steel.

years.big: "We weren't sure if we could still do it. We could still do it."
q: We weren't sure if we could still do it. We could still do it.
years.src: Wikipedia: Jawbreaker (band) · The FADER: After 21 Years, Jawbreaker Is Reuniting To Headline Riot Fest
years.h: Riot Fest announces Jawbreaker as a headliner after 21 years
years.p: Adam Pfahler, on a rehearsal the band held the year before.
years.xp:
Years of reunion denials from Schwarzenbach come first. He had said he did not think he could sing the songs, while Pfahler said he would do it in a heartbeat.

Riot Fest called it a one-time exclusive, with no other dates planned.

yt: Condition Oakland, first show in 21 years
years.h: First reunion show: the Ivy Room, Albany, California
years.p: August 3, 2017, a private show opening for Monsula. First time on stage in 21 years.

years.cap: Jawbreaker at Riot Fest, Chicago, Sept. 17, 2017
years.src: Stereogum: At Riot Fest 2017, Jawbreaker Finally Became Rock Stars
years.h: Riot Fest 2017 gets Jawbreaker on the last night
years.p: They open with "Boxcar" and close with "Bivouac."
years.xp:
Schwarzenbach told the crowd: "Everyone call into work tomorrow, general strike, because fuck this country." He said they were honored to play, then corrected it to humbled.

The crowd was big for a band without radio hits, if smaller than Nine Inch Nails and Wu-Tang Clan. At the end Schwarzenbach tore off his monitor and mangled his guitar, then came back so the crowd could sing the closing refrain, while Pfahler threw his sticks into the audience.

On the video screens: bearded guys bawling during "Condition Oakland."

years.h: Three nights at Brooklyn Steel sell out: the first New York shows in 25 years
years.p: It follows two San Francisco dates in January. Hollywood Palladium comes in March, their first LA shows in 22 years.

years.h: At the Fillmore they play "Gemini," written after Dear You and never recorded
years.p: Over a three-night San Francisco residency they also debut "Black Art," a rearranged Thorns of Life song.

years.cap: Jawbreaker at the Albert Hall, Manchester, UK, April 28, 2019
years.h: First European tour in 25 years, ending in Barcelona
years.p: Stops include Groezrock, Primavera Sound and London's Shepherd's Bush Empire, with Beach Slang supporting on two dates.
years.xp: At a 2019 Q&A for the documentary at Nitehawk in New York, the band said a new 7-inch was slow going, with Bauermeister in Olympia, Pfahler in San Francisco and Schwarzenbach in Brooklyn.

years.cap: Blake Schwarzenbach at the Fillmore, San Francisco, March 2022
years.src: Uproxx: Jawbreaker's Blake Schwarzenbach On 'Dear You' And Touring
years.h: The Dear You anniversary tour plays the album in full
years.p: Twenty-seven dates, with songs the band had not played live before, including "Oyster" and "Unlisted."
years.xp: Schwarzenbach told Uproxx he was excited about the road: cars, sleeping, books, each other and windows.
